oneOf.title: BATCH
oneOf.description: Groups entities by count: puts each arrival in the block's store and, as soon as `batch_size` items are waiting, takes exactly that many atomically to form one batch entity. Members leave live_entities and carry `in_batch` until a SEPARATE splits the batch again. With `max_wait` set, a PARTIAL batch leaves too: the timer is armed by the arrival that starts a new group and releases whatever is waiting once the oldest member has waited that long. TIE RULE: a batch that fills in the same instant as the timer expires wins and the timer releases nothing -- the same zero-delay re-check reneging uses, so the outcome never depends on the order SimPy happened to schedule two events at one timestamp.

oneOf.title: DECIDE
oneOf.description: N-way branch. "Chance" mode draws on the block's own RNG against cumulative `probs`; "Condition" mode evaluates each of `conditions` in order and takes the first true one. Both modes take the last outgoing link as an ELSE branch when there is one more link than probs/conditions; otherwise an uncovered draw or condition fails loud rather than silently dropping the entity. "Policy" mode hands the choice to `ctx.controllers[policy]`: the number of actions is simply the number of outgoing links. A plain (synchronous) controller is called inline, in zero simulated time, exactly like Chance/Condition above. A `PausingController` (used by `nagasim.rl. SimEnv` to drive the policy from outside the run) is different: this block yields on a simpy event instead, so the whole simulation genuinely pauses until something resolves it. With no controller attached for `policy`, the block falls back to `fallback` ("first" / "random" / "shortest") so a Policy-mode model still runs and validates headless.

oneOf.title: RECORD
oneOf.description: RECORD block: a zero-time block that updates a user-defined statistic and forwards the entity unchanged. Statistics live on the simulation context (`ctx.user_stats`), keyed by `stat_name`, so two RECORD blocks writing to the same name share one collector -- core/schema/ rejects a same-name pair with different `kind`s at load time, before a run can hit the mismatch here. `expr` is the increment for "count", the observed value for "tally", the new level for "time_persistent", and ignored for "time_between" (it tallies the gap since the statistic's last arrival; the first arrival records nothing). `kind="cost"` is the one kind that builds no collector: `expr` is a MONEY amount added to the cost item `stat_name` every time an entity passes -- an ordering cost, a changeover cost, a lost-sale penalty. It joins the model's Total Cost and is itemised in the `cost_summary` frame.

cost_item.description: Cost item the lump accrues into; defaults to the record's own name.

components.description: Named components the level's content is tracked in: a gas holder's ch4. Each inflow carries a share, each outflow draws at the level's own blend, and the component is conserved exactly. Read by FRACTION(name, component).

initial_fraction.description: Share of the INITIAL content that is this component.

blend_tolerance.description: How far the fraction may drift from the value the outflows are drawing at before the engine re-evaluates. The crossing instant is solved in closed form; the component is conserved exactly whatever this is set to.

conveyor.description: Makes the stock a Stella conveyor: material rides round(transit_time/dt) slats of the SD grid (euler only), leaves as the one primary outflow (rate "") and may leak on the way through "leak" flows. The stock is the sum of the slats and changes only at grid points.

transit_time.description: Time on the belt, latched per batch at entry.

time_unit.description: Unit `transit_time` is in.

capacity.description: Most the belt holds; limits equation-driven inflow only.

in_limit.description: Most inflow per time unit (equation-driven inflow only).

arrest.description: While nonzero nothing moves, enters or leaves.

leak_kind.description: linear: a batch loses fraction * its entry amount spread evenly over the zone; exponential: content * fraction * dt per DT.

flow.description: A rate-based transfer between levels. The rate is an expression re-evaluated only at events, so every level moves linearly in between and every crossing is solved in closed form.

diagram.description: Position in the stock-and-flow view; ignored by the engine.

dims.description: Subscripts this record runs over: it is flattened into one record per element, named "Name[north]" ("Name[north,young]" for two). Inside, "x[dim]" in a LEVEL/FLOW/AUX/DELAY name reads the same element, and SUM(x)/MEAN(x) aggregate over "x[*]".

elements.description: Per-element equations: {"north": "2", "a,x": "3"} replaces the record's first expression (a level's initial, a flow's rate, an auxiliary's expr, a delay's input) for those elements; the shared one covers the rest. Keys join one element per dim with a comma.

from.description: Level drawn from; omit for a source outside the model. A level at its min passes on no more than flows into it, so a rate needs no guard such as IF(LEVEL("x") > 0, r, 0); on a step grid that guard reads the level a step late.

to.description: Level fed; omit for a sink outside the model.

rate.description: Quantity per time unit: an expression over variables, TS(), TABLE(), LEVEL() and FLOW(). A negative value is clamped to 0 -- declare the reverse flow instead, or set "biflow".

biflow.description: Bi-directional: a negative rate runs the flow backwards instead of being clamped to 0. Both ends must be outside the model or levels with "min": null and no capacity or power limit.

efficiency.description: out = in * efficiency; the rest is a loss.

price.description: Money per unit moved; integrated exactly into the flow's Cost and the model's Total Cost.

emission_factor.description: Impact per unit moved (emissions, water, waste), integrated into Total Impact.

tag.description: Bus tag: every flow carrying it is summed by FLOWSUM("tag"), so a site's generation or demand is one number however many assets contribute to it.

priority.description: Merit order within a tag: FLOWSUM("tag", p) sums only the flows with a priority below p -- what the devices dispatched before this one actually took.

peak_price.description: Demand charge: money per unit of the flow's Peak Rate, billed ONCE at the end of the run. A time-varying tariff is "price".

min_rate.description: Minimum load: the flow runs at 0 or at least this rate, never in between. The gate is applied to the rate the expression ASKED for, before saturation, so it adds no event of its own and cannot chatter.

components.description: Share of what this flow moves that is each component, a number or an expression. Omit a component to carry the SOURCE level's own blend.

leak.description: A conveyor's leakage outflow; set "rate": "" and "from" the conveyor.

fraction.description: Linear: share of a batch lost over the zone. Exponential: rate per time unit. Read every DT.

zone.description: [start, end] fractions of the belt from the inflowing side.

thresholds.description: Realised-rate values that fire discrete logic when crossed : a signal, a variable, and a lump cost per crossing -- a generator's start cost. Rising crossings are counted as the flow's Starts.

cost_item.description: Cost item it accrues into; defaults to the flow's own name.

conversion.description: A delayed conversion with a yield curve: feed in, product released over the following hours or days, per substrate. Feed is grouped into cohorts closed at a fixed interval and each cohort releases at a rate constant within each step of its curve, so the product rate stays piecewise constant. Read by CONV(name) and FRACTION(name, component); attach it to a level with an ordinary flow whose rate is CONV(name).

unit.description: Label for the product, e.g. Nm3.

cohort_interval.description: Feed accumulated over this interval closes into one cohort and releases from its CLOSE, so the mean delay is longer by up to half an interval. Curve knots round onto the same grid.

time_unit.description: Unit the cohort interval and the curve ages are in.

feed.description: Feed rate of this substrate: an expression, usually FLOW of its feeder.

feed_time_unit.description: Unit the feed rate is per.

yield.description: Product per unit of feed, e.g. 200 Nm3 of biogas per tonne.

curve.description: Release curve as [age, CUMULATIVE share] knots, ending at 1.0.

half_life.description: First-order release shortcut, discretised into equal-width steps instead of an explicit curve.

steps.description: Steps the half-life curve is cut into.

tail.description: Half-lives the discretisation spans; the remainder is renormalised in, so the yield is conserved exactly.

components.description: Share of this substrate's product that is each component (a feedstock's methane content). Evaluated once at run start.

initial_inventory.description: Feed already inside at t=0, released as one cohort.

initial_feed_rate.description: Start in the STEADY STATE for this feed rate: the output is feed x yield from t=0, so a year-long study needs no start-up transient.

fixed_cost.description: A cost of the SCENARIO rather than of the run: capex, or an annuity over a sized parameter. The amount is evaluated once at run start, joins Total Cost and is itemised in the cost_summary frame. It is never prorated to the observed window -- write the share you want into the expression.

amount.description: A number, or an expression over the model's variables and data evaluated once at run start.

category.description: Grouping shown in the cost_summary frame.

capex.description: An upfront investment: the investment case keeps it out of operating cost. Read by `nagasim.investment` only; Total Cost and every frame of a run are unchanged.

investment.description: OPTIONAL investment case: `naga invest` and the Studies window report payback, NPV and ROI of every scenario against the baseline. Per replication the run's Total Cost less its capex fixed costs, and the throughput, are scaled from the observed window to operating_hours_per_year.

baseline.description: A scenario name; empty is the model as saved.

horizon_years.description: Years the saving is counted over; a fraction counts its last year pro rata.

operating_hours_per_year.description: The observed window is scaled to this.

margin_per_part.description: Money per extra good part; 0 is a pure cost case.

throughput.description: A KPI key counting good parts (a `flatten_kpis` key such as "user/Good parts"); empty is the system's completed entities.

subscript.description: A dimension: a record with "dims": [name] is flattened into one record per element when the model is built.

name.description: An identifier, written as "[name]" in a lookup.

parent.description: Makes this a subrange of that dimension: its elements are a subset of the parent's. "x[North]" reads the owner's element inside an owner over North or its parent; SUM(x[North*]) sums the subset.

map_to.description: Maps this dimension element-wise onto another : inside an owner over this one, "x[dim]" reads the corresponding element (and the reverse when it is one-to-one).

elements.description: The target element of each element, in order; absent maps by position (same size).

auxiliary.description: A named expression read as AUX("name"): evaluated on read, memoised per pass of the level engine. A flow reading an auxiliary that reads LEVEL() or TNOW is re-integrated on the SD grid.

dims.description: Subscripts this record runs over: it is flattened into one record per element, named "Name[north]" ("Name[north,young]" for two). Inside, "x[dim]" in a LEVEL/FLOW/AUX/DELAY name reads the same element, and SUM(x)/MEAN(x) aggregate over "x[*]".

elements.description: Per-element equations: {"north": "2", "a,x": "3"} replaces the record's first expression (a level's initial, a flow's rate, an auxiliary's expr, a delay's input) for those elements; the shared one covers the rest. Keys join one element per dim with a comma.

expr.description: Any flow-rate expression; may call AUX() of another auxiliary (no cycles) and the inline delays.

diagram.description: Position in the stock-and-flow view; ignored by the engine.

delay.description: A delay read as DELAY("name"). material: n stages each drained at S/(tau/n), the output is the outflow; information (SMOOTH): n stages chasing the input, the output is the last; both need simulation.sd. pipeline (DELAYP): the input exactly tau later, no grid needed. sample (SAMPLE_IF_TRUE): holds the last input read while condition was true, initial before the first true reading -- "input"/"delay_time" do not apply, use "condition"/"input". noise (NOISE_NORMAL): a normal draw clipped to [lo, hi], redrawn once per re-evaluation from a stream fixed by this delay's own name (CRN) -- use "mean"/"sd"/"lo"/"hi" instead of "input"/"delay_time"; refused under RK4. Inline SMOOTH/SMOOTH3/DELAY1/DELAY3/DELAYN/DELAYP/INITIAL/ACTIVE_INITIAL/SAMPLE_IF_TRUE/TREND/FORECAST/NPV/NOISE_NORMAL calls in a level's initial value, a flow rate, an auxiliary or a delay field are shorthand for these records (INITIAL becomes a hidden level, not a delay).

dims.description: Subscripts this record runs over: it is flattened into one record per element, named "Name[north]" ("Name[north,young]" for two). Inside, "x[dim]" in a LEVEL/FLOW/AUX/DELAY name reads the same element, and SUM(x)/MEAN(x) aggregate over "x[*]".

elements.description: Per-element equations: {"north": "2", "a,x": "3"} replaces the record's first expression (a level's initial, a flow's rate, an auxiliary's expr, a delay's input) for those elements; the shared one covers the rest. Keys join one element per dim with a comma.

input.description: What is delayed: a rate for a material delay, a value otherwise; the sampled value for "sample" (required for every kind but "noise").

delay_time.description: tau, in the model's base time unit (> 0); a pipeline reads it once at run start. Required for material/information/pipeline only.

initial.description: The output at t=0 (not "noise", which has none).

diagram.description: Position in the stock-and-flow view; ignored by the engine.

oneOf.title: set
oneOf.description: Set self.<attribute> or a model variable to an expression's value.

oneOf.title: send
oneOf.description: Send a message, delivered at the same instant (FIFO); the receiving transition reads `payload`.

oneOf.title: enter
oneOf.description: Create an entity at a block; entity.agent is this agent.

oneOf.title: transfer
oneOf.description: Move an amount into or out of a level (the TRANSFER block's instant move).

oneOf.title: signal
oneOf.description: Raise a signal, releasing every HOLD (mode Signal) waiting on it.

oneOf.title: move_to
oneOf.description: Move at the type's `speed` to a point, a network node or another agent; arrival delivers an "arrived" message. A literal [x, y] point, or an expression: a string constant ("'dock'") for a node, [x, y] for a computed point, AGENT("Pop", i) for another agent.

oneOf.title: spawn
oneOf.description: Add agents to a population: count (default 1) and the init expressions are evaluated in the spawner's scope; a newborn starts in state (default its type's initial state), its own attribute inits run first. More than the population's max_count alive at once stops the run (E_POPULATION_FULL).

oneOf.title: remove
oneOf.description: Remove agents: "self" ends the firing there; any send target works. A ref kept to a removed agent raises when used; ALIVE(ref) tests it.

oneOf.title: step
oneOf.description: Grid only: move by [dx, dy] whole cells, instantly; off the edge of a non-torus grid the agent stays.

oneOf.title: move_random
oneOf.description: Grid only: to a neighbourhood cell drawn uniformly from the agent's own stream; "free": only cells holding no agent of its population (none: it stays).

oneOf.title: link
oneOf.description: Link self to each target (agents of its own population; self is skipped).

oneOf.title: unlink
oneOf.description: Drop self's links to each target ("links": all).

oneOf.title: python
oneOf.description: Call fn(agent, api), a top-level def in the type's `python`. Runs only with the caller's consent (NAGASIM_ALLOW_AGENT_PYTHON=1); a model file cannot grant it.

oneOf.title: forward
oneOf.description: Move `self.heading` degrees' worth forward by an expression's distance; a continuous space only.

oneOf.title: turn
oneOf.description: Add an expression's degrees to `self.heading`; a continuous space only.

oneOf.title: face
oneOf.description: Set `self.heading` toward a point, a network node or another agent -- the same target shapes as move_to.

oneOf.title: random_walk
oneOf.description: Move forward by "step", after turning by NORM(0, turn_sd) degrees (default 0, a straight walk).

agent_target.description: "self", an index in the sender's population, an expression giving an agent (AGENT("Pop", i), entity.agent), or a population with an optional condition on the recipient and a random pick; "links" or {"links": true, ...}, self's linked neighbours instead of a population.

agent_tick.description: A fixed-step schedule, ticks at phase + k * dt (k an integer, strictly after the run start). synchronous: every agent reads the tick-start state (on_tick for all, then tick transitions for all); random: a fresh permutation per tick; sequential: index order. A population's keys override its type's.

time_unit.description: Unit `dt` and `phase` are in.

parent.description: The composite state this one nests in; a state is composite iff another names it here.

initial.description: Composite only: the child entered first (default: its first child in declaration order).

diagram.description: Editor position; ignored by the engine.

agent_transition.description: Exactly one trigger: timeout (a duration from entry), rate (per agent per time unit: shared, own or own * shared), condition (re-checked after each agent event), message (a name, "" for any; guard and actions read `payload`) or tick (a condition checked at each of the population's ticks, "" for every tick).

scan.description: Re-check a rate or condition every scan time units (for inputs that move outside the agents).

history.description: Composite target only: re-enter at the child (shallow) or leaf (deep) it was left in.

agent_type.description: A statechart run for every agent of a population; parameters are names in its expressions, self.<attribute> reads the agent's own columns (plus self.state, self.id).

anyOf.description: Row i of the population's own table for agent i.

kind.description: "category" stores init/set as one of "categories" (a closed set); self.<attr> reads back the category name.

anyOf.description: Continuous 2D bounds, or the model's own "network" section; A grid of cells with patches.

edge.description: Continuous only: what a move_to/forward/random_walk step does at the bounds -- pass through, clamp inside, wrap to the opposite edge, or bounce the heading.

cell.description: Grid only: a cell's side; agents sit at cell centres ((cx + 0.5) * cell, ...).

neighbourhood.description: Grid only: the 8 or 4 cells NEIGHBOURS, move_random and diffuse use.

patches.description: Grid only: per-cell values read by PATCH("name"[, dx, dy]) and written by a set of "patch.<name>".

init.description: A number, or an expression of cx, cy (e.g. TABLE(...)).

grow.description: Each patch tick a cell below max gains rate, clipped at max (default: its initial value).

patch_tick.description: Grid only: every patch diffuses, evaporates, then grows at k * patch_tick.

time_unit.description: Unit `patch_tick` is in.

speed.description: An expression (self, parameters, constants) a move_to evaluates once, in the space's own units per time unit.

let.description: Tick-local values, {name: expression}, evaluated in order once per agent per tick before on_tick; read as a bare name by on_tick and the tick transitions.

on_tick.description: Actions every agent runs at each tick, before its tick transitions.

python.description: Def statements only; {python: <fn>} actions call fn(agent, api). Parsed at validation, never run there; a run needs the caller's consent (NAGASIM_ALLOW_AGENT_PYTHON=1).

anyOf.description: The number of rows of a model table (one agent per row), or the sum of one of its columns (a group table).

max_count.description: The most agents alive at once when spawn actions add some (>= count); default count.

network.description: The initial links between this population's agents, drawn at run start from its own network stream. random: G(n, p) (p, or mean_degree = p (n - 1)); small_world: Watts-Strogatz ring of k neighbours, each link rewired with probability beta; scale_free: Barabasi-Albert, m links per new agent; table: a model table's "from"/"to" columns (agent indices); none: no initial links.

link_on_spawn.description: A newborn starts linked to the agent of this population that spawned it.

color_by.description: A declared categorical attribute; playback colours the population's tokens by its current category instead of by state (2D and 3D).

colors.description: {category: colour name}, the palette color_by draws from -- the same names a statechart state's own "color" uses. Presentational only, like that field.

initial.description: The first agents by index start in these states, the rest in the type's initial state.

placement.description: Only meaningful when the type has a space: default {"kind": "random"} (uniform over the space's own bounds, or a uniform random network node, both from the agent's own stream).

bounds.description: Overrides the space's own bounds (continuous, kind random).

points.description: [[x, y], ...], one per agent by index, cycled (continuous, kind table); on a grid, cells [cx, cy].

nodes.description: Network node names, one per agent by index, cycled (network, kind table).

sequence.description: A routing: an ordered list of operations a product follows through STATION blocks. A ROUTE block sends an entity whose `sequence` attribute names this one to each step's station in turn, assigning that step's "values" as entity attributes on the way.

station.description: Name of a STATION block; inside a submodel instance that is the flattened "instance/station" path.

values.description: Attributes assigned to the entity when it is sent to this step, e.g. {"process_time": 3}.

network.description: The path network: nodes at real layout coordinates and the segments joining them. Travel between two places is the shortest path along the segments, so a distance is geometry, not a guess.

length_factor.description: Multiplies the straight-line distance when a segment declares no explicit length. 1.0 is straight aisles.

capacity.description: Recorded, not enforced in this build.

length.description: Null takes the straight-line distance x length_factor.

speed.description: Speed LIMIT on this segment; it changes travel time, never the route chosen.

capacity.description: Vehicles allowed on it at once (zone control, both directions of a two-way segment together); null is unlimited .

motion_profile.description: How something moves (automation sub-project 1): a robot, a person or a mechanism, named by a MOTION block's `profile`. The rules are the same for every kind.

payload_max.description: kg; null or absent = no payload derating.

payload_derate.description: Speed fraction at payload_max, linear from 1.0 at 0 kg.

collaborative_speed.description: m/s; required when a block uses hrc "collaborative" or "separation".

fleet.description: A pool of vehicles that carry entities on the network. A fleet IS a resource under its own name, so schedules, failures, utilization and costs all work on it unchanged.

kind.description: "worker" lets a SEIZE/PROCESS summon a unit with `worker_fleet`; the pool is unchanged.

motion.description: "gantry" travels directly between two nodes' coordinates (`speed_x`/`speed_y`/`hoist_time`), ignoring the path network and segment capacity; cannot be kind "worker".

speed_x.description: Gantry only: speed along x, distance per model time unit.

speed_y.description: Gantry only: speed along y, distance per model time unit.

hoist_time.description: Gantry only: fixed time added to every hop (raising and lowering the load), in `time_unit`.

home.description: Node this unit starts at and parks at; defaults to the fleet's `home`.

loads.description: Entities one vehicle may carry on a tour: up to loads - 1 waiting TRANSPORTs ride with the one granted the vehicle. 1 on a worker fleet.

arm.description: Name of a `motion_profiles` record: the fleet is a mobile cobot, which loads and unloads a STATION that declares `tending` with its arm. Empty or absent: an ordinary fleet. Needs kind "vehicle", motion "network" and loads 1.

exchange.description: Arm fleets only: a second holding place, so a cobot arriving loaded at a machine that holds a finished part picks it, places its own and carries the finished one on.

speed.description: Loaded speed, distance per model time unit.

speed_unit.description: Unit of every speed of the fleet.

speed_empty.description: Speed when driving to a pick-up; defaults to `speed`.

time_unit.description: Unit the load and unload times are in.

home.description: Node the vehicles start at, and return to under `park: "home"`.

capacity_schedule.description: A "capacity"-kind schedule: how many vehicles are on shift.

dispatch.description: Whose request is served when a vehicle frees. Priority is the primary key under both.

select.description: Which idle vehicle serves a granted request.

power.description: kW per vehicle while busy/idle/blocked/down/off_shift; absent keys are 0, "blocked" defaults to "busy" (a blocked vehicle is seized).

graphic.description: Inline SVG vehicle picture (24 x 24 artboard, facing east) drawn for each unit on the floor plan; the editor's generic vehicle when absent.

length_m.description: Vehicle length in metres for the floor-plan marker (default 2.4).

battery.description: Each vehicle carries a battery: it drains at the fleet's `power` kW per state and recharges at a charger. State of charge (SoC) values are fractions, 0 to 1.

initial.description: SoC at the start of the run.

low.description: A vehicle freed below this SoC goes to charge.

opportunity_below.description: Opportunity only: an idle vehicle below it charges when a point is free, and stays dispatchable.

schedule.description: Scheduled only: a `schedules` record; vehicles freed while its value is > 0 charge until `target` or the window's end.

chargers.description: Chargers the fleet may use; default every charger of the kind its strategy needs.

charger.description: A charger or a battery-swap station at a network node (automation sub-project 2), used by fleets that declare a `battery`.

node.description: The network node it stands at.

power_kw.description: kW per point; for "swap", the rate a removed pack recharges at.

knee.description: Above this SoC the power falls linearly.

spare_packs.description: Swap only: charged packs in stock at the start; a swap waits for one. Absent = unlimited.

scenario.description: A named set of parameter overrides applied to the base model.

reality_check.description: A Vensim-style reality check: a test input imposed on the model (a scenario-style override map), then a constraint the model is expected to keep. Run by `nagasim.modelcheck`, one deterministic replication per check.

inputs.description: Override path -> value, the same grammar a scenario override's "path" uses (e.g. "auxiliaries.Workforce.expr": "0").

constraint.description: A boolean expression over LEVEL()/AUX()/FLOW() and TNOW, checked at every sampled instant the "when" below selects.

when.description: "always" (every sample), "final" (the last sample only) or "after <t>" (samples at or after time t).

assertion.description: A model assertion: pins one KPI (an `experiments.flatten_kpis` key) against a comparison operator and value, checked over its own replications by a Student-t confidence interval. Run by `nagasim.modelcheck.check`, `naga check`.

kpi.description: A KPI key from `experiments.flatten_kpis`, e.g. "system/Throughput (per time unit)" or "resource/Server/Usage % (snapshot)".

op.description: Passes when the WHOLE confidence interval clears the bound ("==" means inside value +/- tolerance).

replications.description: Assertions sharing a replication count are run in one batch.

tolerance.description: Half-width of the "==" band around value; ignored by the other operators.

dashboard_widget.description: A dashboard widget: kpi/gauge read one expression, line/bar read 1-4/1-8 labelled series, sampled at the same instants as the timeseries sampler (`core/timeseries.py`). "row"/"col"/"span" are layout hints for the editor's dashboard panel only.

series.description: line/bar only: 1-4 series for a line widget, 1-8 for a bar.

thresholds.description: gauge only: ascending values within [min, max].

dashboard_control.description: A game-mode control: a slider sets a resource's capacity (within 0..its declared capacity), a variable or an SD auxiliary over [min, max]; a decision answers the pending decision of a Policy-mode DECIDE, one option label per outgoing link.

target.description: slider only: exactly one of capacity (a resource), variable, constant (an SD auxiliary).

policy.description: decision only: a Policy-mode DECIDE's policy.

options.description: decision only: one label per outgoing link.

dashboard_input.description: Present mode: one value a viewer may change before a run, as an override of "path" checked by `nagasim.dashboard.input_overrides`: a number within [min, max], a switch (true/false) or one of the listed choices; never text. Not `simulation.seed` or `simulation.replications`. Whether the path addresses something of this kind in the model is reported when the dashboard is used (`nagasim.dashboard.check_inputs`, `E_DASHBOARD_INPUT`), not by `naga validate`.

max.description: number only; greater than min, at most 10000 steps away.

step.description: number only; a hint for the control.

dashboard_result.description: Present mode: a KPI to report first, by its `experiments.flatten_kpis` key. The keys depend on the run, so only the shape is checked.

dashboard_page.description: Present mode: one page of the Presenter. The item kinds a page takes depend on its activity: what_if: input, result, widget, table, view; scenarios: scenarios, result, widget, table, view; play: view, decisions, control, widget, result, table. Positions are hints.

ref.description: input: its path; result: its kpi; widget and control: its name.

dashboard.description: The dashboard: KPI tiles, gauges, time charts and bars over the model's own expression language, shown during playback and in the results. Since v29 also what Present mode shows a person who did not build the model: "inputs", "results", "limits" and "pages"; with no "pages" the definition is generated (`nagasim.dashboard.default_dashboard`). Absent for a model that declares none.

limits.description: What a run on a viewer's behalf may cost.

hidden.description: Generated entries the author removed ("input:<path>", "result:<kpi>", "page:<name>"): regenerating never adds them back.

annotation.description: A canvas note or frame; the engine ignores this section.

submodel.description: A reusable definition, instantiated by a SUBMODEL block and flattened away before the engine sees the model.

type.description: What the argument is. A string value is an EXPRESSION unless the type is a literal one (name/choice/string), where the word itself is the value.

refers_to.description: For type "name": the kind of record the argument names (resource, resource_set, schedule, table, sequence, entity).

extends.description: Inherit another definition: this one is the parent's with its own blocks and parameters merged in by name (child wins), links by source/target/ports, `scoped` per record. Chains allowed; a cycle is E_EXTENDS_CYCLE.

remove.description: With `extends`: parent blocks to drop, with every parent link touching one; a `src->tgt` entry drops the parent links between those two blocks.

data_source.description: Where a data binding reads from. A relative `location` resolves against the MODEL FILE's folder; `sql`/`json_url` are refused unless the caller explicitly allows network access, and a literal password in a URL is a validation error (use "${NAGASIM_DATA_<NAME>}").

location.description: Path relative to the model file, or a URL. For a live kind: what to read over the connection (a path), never a host.

connection.description: Live kinds only: the NAME of a connection the person running the model defined in their own connections file. A model never holds an address or a credential.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, for the xlsx kind.

options.description: Extra keyword arguments for the pandas reader; for a live kind, that reader's own options.

data_binding.description: One model parameter read from a data source.

filter.description: {"column": value} or {"column >=": value}; comparisons only, never code.

transform.description: One of mean, median, last, sum, count, value, fit, empirical, orders, or quantile:<argument>, rate_per:<argument>, arrival_schedule:<argument>, table:<argument>, series:<argument>.

map.description: "orders" transform only: {order field: source column} for any field whose column is not already named after it.

order.description: A released job: what a CREATE block in "Orders" arrival mode emits at `release`, carrying a due date the run reports lateness and tardiness against. Times are in the model's BASE unit.

id.description: Unique; the KPI frames report the order under it.

release.description: When the order is released into the model. An ISO timestamp instead of a number needs a calendar.

due.description: Absolute due time, not a lead time; null = no due date. May be an ISO timestamp.

time_unit.description: Unit `release` and `due` are in (a dated value ignores it).

entity_type.description: Overrides the CREATE block's own e_type.

sequence.description: Name of a declared routing the entities follow.

source.description: CREATE block that releases it; omit for the first CREATE in "Orders" mode.

attributes.description: Further attributes assigned onto every entity of this order.

plan.description: {station: planned start}, carried as entity.plan and read by the "Plan" queue discipline (cpsat.propose writes it).

initial_state.description: Warm start: what is already in the system at t=0.

time.description: Timestamp of the snapshot this state came from; recorded for the report, never shifts the clock.

time_unit.description: Unit `time` is in.

clock.description: The model time the run's clock starts at (default 0): the time a state was taken at. Statistics cover the run from there, as after a warm-up of that length.

schedule_offset.description: How far into its own cycle the calendar already is at model time 0, in base time units. Every schedule and every repeating time-series input is read at t + this, so a mid-shift warm start resumes the shift instead of restarting it.

arrivals.description: Per CREATE block: the arrivals already made and the absolute time of the next one.

scheduled.description: When the next arrival was drawn.

rank.description: Its place among arrivals drawn at one instant for one instant.

orders.description: Per declared order released before the clock: the entities it released and completed, and when the last one completed.

resource_sets.description: Per resource set: the index of the member a Cyclical set picked last (-1: none yet).

blocks.description: Per block, what it carries: a changeover's setup key its last job left; a BATCH's running maximum wait, the time it falls due; a CONVEYOR's next free entry slot.

variables.description: Model variable values to start from.

fleets.description: Where each vehicle of a fleet is: one record per unit, in unit order. Times are absolute.

cursor.description: The unit a fleet with select "cyclic" picked last, -1 for none.

node.description: The network node it stands at, or left from when it drives.

until.description: When its loading or unloading ends.

levels.description: Level values to start from: the state of charge of a battery, the stock on hand in a warehouse.

used.description: The resources, sets and stores something happened to before the clock: they keep their report row.

block.description: The block to inject into; a block inside a submodel is "<instance>/<inner>".

age.description: Time already spent in the system before t=0.

ends.description: Instead of `remaining`: the absolute time each service in progress ends.

auto_cost.description: The part of the entity's `cost` attribute the engine charged itself.

member.description: The member of the block's resource set serving the entry's jobs in service.

deadline.description: The absolute time the entry's waiting entities give up (a block with renege_after).

since.description: The absolute time the entry's waiting entities joined the queue (at or before the clock): their wait counts from it.

arrives.description: The absolute time an entity on a link reaches the block (count 1).

held_by.description: The block that still holds a waiting entity: the BUFFER whose place it has, or the station blocked after service that keeps its unit until the entity is accepted, or the CONVEYOR whose end keeps it until the next belt takes it (count 1).

held_since.description: The absolute time the station in held_by seized its unit, or the entity entered the belt in held_by.

holds.description: Resources the entity holds from an earlier block, seized again for it before anything else: per resource or set, since when, how many units (default 1) and of a set which member.

belt.description: An entity on an accumulating CONVEYOR: its stage (cell: waits for a cell; slot: boards at until; ride: at the end at until; packed: behind the part ahead; move: moving up, there at until; stop: waits for the end stop), until, and when it entered the belt.

place.description: false: the entity waits for a place of the block (a BUFFER, a queue_capacity) and has none yet.

trip.description: A load's trip, at its TRANSPORT block: the origin and destination nodes, the target STATION block and, once a vehicle has it, its unit, the stage (pickup, load, carry, unload) and the unload time already drawn.

down_until.description: Absolute time, or an ISO timestamp with a calendar.

busy.description: An observation: the units reported busy. It must match the entities in service.

failures.description: Per failure name: {"next": t}, the absolute time it fails, or {"down_until": t or null}, down by it now and repaired at t.

simulation.description: Run settings; every one can be overridden per run.

time_limit.description: Run length in base time units; null/0 means "run until the model drains", which only works for a model that can drain.

warmup.description: Statistics are reset at this time.

deterministic.description: Deterministic run mode: every distribution samples its mean, DECIDE-by-chance uses largest-remainder allocation, a failure's TTF/TTR use their mean, and replications are forced to 1. A mean-value model, not a fluid limit; agent-based and system-dynamics parts are unaffected.

time_unit.description: The model's BASE unit; every duration without its own unit is already in it.

length_unit.description: The model's length unit: default unit of new length fields and of reported lengths.

currency.description: Cost label only; never enters the arithmetic.

energy_price.description: Money per kWh, a number or an expression, evaluated once at run start. Prices every resource/fleet's "power".

record_logs.description: Record the per-EVENT entity/resource/store logs . False returns the three flat log frames empty and leaves every summary statistic exact -- what a big study wants.

timeseries_points.description: How many samples the time-series OUTPUT sampler takes over a time-limited run (default 200).

timeseries_interval.description: Fixed sampling interval for a draining run, which has no horizon to divide.

timeseries_counts.description: Blocks whose departures the sampler counts, as the series block/<name>/out (flattened names). What a twin compares a plant counter with; none by default.

sd.description: OPTIONAL system-dynamics step grid. Absent, rates change only at events. Present, every rate reading LEVEL(), FRACTION() or TNOW is re-integrated at each multiple of "dt"; static rates and events inside a step stay exact.

method.description: euler, or rk4 as an effective rate over each step (no random draws in a dynamic rate).

time_unit.description: Unit dt is in.

calendar.description: OPTIONAL real dates. Absent, the clock is a plain number and nothing changes. Present, model time 0 is "start" and weekday schedules, dated series and dated orders resolve against it.

start.description: ISO 8601 instant model time 0 stands for. With no offset it is read in "timezone", never in the machine's local time.

timezone.description: IANA name (Europe/Rome). The wall clock weekday schedules and date labels use.

end.description: Run until this instant, instead of a "time_limit" length.
